Designed and implemented a contract analysis chatbot using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to help users review, interpret, and summarize legal documents with the assistance of AI. The system allows users to upload contracts and receive context-aware, evidence-backed answers to questions about clauses, risks, and obligations.

It also provides summaries and compliance insights, significantly reducing the time and effort required for manual document review.

AI powered Interview Coach
This project is an advanced AI-driven interview preparation platform designed to help users build confidence and improve their performance in any interview scenario. It enables candidates to practice interactively with an AI interviewer across three modes — chat, audio, and video — providing a realistic and adaptive simulation experience.
Powered by a combination of cutting-edge technologies, including OpenAI’s language models, Google Cloud, AssemblyAI, embeddings, and PostgreSQL, the system generates tailored interview questions based on the user’s target role or industry. During each session, it delivers real-time feedback and analysis on the user’s responses, assessing communication clarity, relevance, tone, and confidence.
Once the session is complete, the platform provides a comprehensive performance evaluation, summarizing key strengths and areas for improvement. A personal analytics dashboard visualizes overall progress over time, allowing users to track their growth, identify skill gaps, and prepare more strategically.
By combining natural language processing, speech recognition, and interactive UX design, this AI-powered coach offers an innovative, data-driven approach to professional development and interview readiness.

Developed an AI-powered chatbot integration for Redash, a leading data visualization and analytics tool. This chatbot allows users to query and explore datasets using natural language, removing the need for complex SQL queries or manual filtering.
The system leverages LLM technology, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) principles, and Python-based backend integration to interpret user intent and translate queries into actionable data requests. Spotting the difference between copper and steel scrap on a fast-moving conveyor belt isn't easy especially when metallic glare ruins your features. ✨
I'm excited to share the results of an end-to-end instance segmentation pipeline I built to automate industrial material sorting.
To bypass thousands of hours of manual polygon drawing, I engineered an automated pseudo-labeling bootstrapping pipeline:
1️⃣ Used SAM 3 (Segment Anything Model) in a zero-shot mode, leveraging its Decoupled Presence Head to perfectly isolate individual, tightly packed metal pieces from each other and the belt texture.
2️⃣ Passed those crisp geometric segments through a custom pre-trained YOLO classifier to instantly stamp them as "Copper" or "Steel".
3️⃣ Compiled the unified boundaries straight into standardized YOLO segmentation syntax.
With a robust training pipeline locked in, I benchmarked several next-gen architectures under identical conditions. Ultimately, the optimized YOLOv8n-seg model emerged as the clear winner—achieving a massive 0.9019 Box mAP50 and 0.8808 Seg mAP50 on highly complex, multi-object production scenes.
For production-scale environments, pairing this highly lightweight, high-precision architecture with dedicated edge-GPU hardware ensures incredibly smooth, lightning-fast inference.
Take a look at how precisely the model maps out the instances!

Working with DXF files in FreeCAD whether importing customer drawings, laser-cutting profiles, or legacy CAD data, hidden geometry can quickly turn into a frustrating troubleshooting exercise.
One of the most common symptoms is the dreaded "Wire not closed" error. You derive your sketch from the source, it looks fully closed, fully constrained, and everything is green, but operations still fail.
A common cause is duplicate or obscured geometry in the DXF, such as one line sitting directly on top of another. These issues aren't always obvious and can lead to a lot of wasted time tracking down the problem.
The Elements List is one of FreeCAD's most overlooked features, but it's incredibly useful for identifying duplicate geometry while preserving your sketch constraints.
In this video I demonstrate a simple workflow for finding and fixing these issue using the Validate Sketch tool and the Elements List.
If you regularly work with imported DXF files, converting them to a sketch then this post process workflow could save you a lot of frustration, and a lot of time.

A handmade welded prototype is rarely built from perfect geometry. Rebuilding it in CAD requires a clear reverse engineering strategy.
In our latest workflow video, we take a rough handmade nozzle from 3D scan data to a clean, editable CAD model in
QUICKSURFACE
.
The workflow covers:
🔸 Extracting key reference geometry from the scan
🔸 Aligning the mesh using symmetry and reference features
🔸 Rebuilding the base fitting
🔸 Extracting the curved pipe centerline
🔸 Defining and sweeping the nozzle geometry
🔸 Trimming, joining, and creating the final slash cut
🔸 Preparing the finished CAD model for export and manufacturing
This is a practical example of how scan data can be used to reconstruct handmade, welded, and irregular prototypes where the original design data is unavailable.

Your 28 Gbps serial link passes simulation. Eye wide open. BER below 1e-15.
Prototype arrives. Eye half closed. Jitter margin gone. Link fails.
The problem is not your design. It's the glass weave in the PCB.
In a differential pair, one trace may fall over a glass bundle (Dk ≈ 6.0), the other over a resin pocket (Dk ≈ 3.0). Propagation delay difference → skew → jitter → eye closure.
Measured skews up to 60 ps have been documented. At 28 Gbps, the UI is 36 ps. A 10 ps skew already collapses the eye.
Distinguishing glass weave jitter from random jitter:
→ Jitter histogram: bimodal or broadened → DJ; Gaussian → RJ
→ Channel‑to‑channel variation: varies across channels → glass weave; consistent → system‑level
→ Jitter spectrum: broad spectral content related to weave pitch → glass weave; sharp peaks → periodic sources
→ Eye/bathtub: asymmetric closure → glass weave; symmetric → RJ
→ Layout correlation: long, straight, parallel‑to‑edge routing on coarse glass → signature
Mitigation:
→ Spread glass or fine glass (106 style) over coarse weaves (2116)
→ Route at 10‑15° angle to weave
→ Widen traces to average over multiple bundles
→ Reduce parallel routing length

By calculating true volume rather than just offsetting existing polygons, these updates allow you to generate clean, watertight geometry effortlessly.
Here is a look at what is new:
🔹 The All-New Sweep Tool: Create complex, intersecting profiles with zero non-manifold geometry using the new Solid Mode.
🔹 Improved Add Thickness: Generate reliable wall thicknesses and clean shells, ideal for highly detailed meshes and organic models.
🔹 Enhanced Bevel Tools: Execute flawless chamfers and fillets on irregular topology without stretched polygons, gaps, or distortion.

Buckling shapes you probably haven’t seen before.
This started as two simple structural models:
• A slender frame
• A meshed shell
I connected them, applied compression, and let geometric nonlinearity take over.
The result is this unusual elastic post-buckling shape.
Small changes to the geometry, stiffness, or connection can produce a completely different response. That sensitivity is what makes nonlinear analysis so fascinating.
